quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: Why is it important to keep space between your vehicle and others?

options.text: It prevents distractions from other vehicles.
It gives you time to react to surprises.
It keeps traffic moving at safe speeds.
It keeps other drivers alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react to surprises.
questions.explanation: Space between your vehicle and others gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Keep driving in your lane.
Move to the right and stop.
Stop immediately where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights or hear a siren, pull to the right side of the road and stop right away.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, you should:

options.text: Use your horn.
Wave your arms.
Turn on your emergency lights.
Flash your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your horn.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who may not see you, like when another driver is about to hit you.

questions.question: To use a roundabout correctly, drivers should:

options.text: Stop inside the roundabout.
Yield to cars entering the roundabout.
Drive in a clockwise direction.
Yield to cars already in the roundabout.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to cars already in the roundabout.
questions.explanation: At a roundabout, enter from the right and yield to traffic already in the roundabout. Follow the circle to the right until you reach your exit.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Slippery when wet.
Tow-away zone.
Steep downgrade.
Construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs with black markings tell drivers about hazards ahead. This sign warns you that the road may become slippery when wet.

questions.question: If law enforcement stops you, you should:

options.text: Stop in the middle of the road.
Move to the right side of the road.
Move to the left side of the road.
Stop wherever you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Park as far to the right as possible. If you can, use the shoulder or a nearby safe side street away from busy traffic.

questions.question: At a flashing red light, you should:

options.text: Stop completely, then go when safe.
Stop only if other cars are approaching.
Stop only if other cars are in the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, yield to other traffic, and go when it is safe.

questions.question: When passing other vehicles, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Move back into your lane within 10 feet of the other car.
You don't need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Return to your lane only when you can see the other car's front in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: Which offense will automatically suspend your license?

options.text: Racing on a public road
Graffiti
Letting someone else use your license
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Your license can be automatically suspended for racing on public roads, graffiti, or letting another person use your license.

questions.question: How alcohol affects your reflexes and judgment:

options.text: Is less serious when drinking beer instead of wine.
Is less serious when drinking wine instead of beer.
Is worst when drinking hard ciders and mixed drinks.
Depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.correctAnswerText: Depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.
questions.explanation: Any type of alcohol can hurt your reflexes and judgment. The type of drink doesn't matter—only the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream.

questions.question: When you approach a roundabout, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Keep the same speed.
Stop completely.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When you approach a roundabout, slow down. Roundabouts are designed for low-speed driving.

questions.question: How can drivers prevent highway hypnosis?

options.text: Move your eyes across the road instead of staring.
Stop every 100 miles to stretch.
Drive no more than eight hours in one day.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis is drowsiness caused by the steady sounds and lack of activity while driving. Prevent it by moving your eyes while driving, stopping every 100 miles to stretch, and limiting driving to eight hours per day.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at the same time to a four-way stop sign intersection, who goes first?

options.text: The driver on the right.
The driver on the left.
One driver can go without stopping.
One driver should honk to say they are giving up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, if you arrive at the same time as another driver, yield to the driver on your right. You can then go when it is safe.

questions.question: Traffic lanes moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.

options.text: Yellow
White
Red
Black

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going in the same direction. Solid white lines cannot be crossed. Broken white lines can be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions.

questions.question: When you enter a street from a driveway, what must you do?

options.text: Drive slowly so vehicles and pedestrians have time to move.
Honk your horn to warn vehicles and pedestrians.
Stop and only go when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
Ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and only go when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the road from a driveway. Yield to all approaching vehicles and crossing pedestrians. The stop must be made before you cross the sidewalk. Not stopping is against the law.

questions.question: Mixing drugs with alcohol:

options.text: Increases the chance of a crash.
Is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.
Makes alcohol's effects weaker.
Does not affect your driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the chance of a crash.
questions.explanation: Drugs (illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter) can harm your brain function and safe driving. Mixing drugs with alcohol greatly increases your crash risk.

questions.question: If you stop at a railroad crossing with more than one track, when should you go?

options.text: When you can see clearly down all the tracks.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go as soon as the train passes.
Go when one track is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see clearly down all the tracks.
questions.explanation: At a multi-track railroad crossing, do not move until you can see clearly down all tracks. Even with one track, wait and check again for another train before crossing.

questions.question: Why is it important to watch for motorcycles?

options.text: They are harder to see than cars.
They rarely use their headlights.
Motorcyclists are less skilled than other drivers.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and hard to see. They can hide in your car's blind spot. It is difficult to judge distance and speed with motorcycles, so always be alert and careful around them.

questions.question: What is the main danger shown by this sign?

options.text: Your headlights will be misaligned because one side of your car is higher.
Your tire could be damaged by drifting onto the shoulder.
You could hydroplane if there is water on the shoulder.
You could lose control if you drift onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You could lose control if you drift onto the shoulder.
questions.explanation: This sign means the shoulder is lower than the road. If a wheel drops onto the low shoulder, do not brake hard or steer sharply. This will cause you to lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: Before turning left, what is most important?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Yield to oncoming vehicles.
Swing to the right side of your lane.
Wait for the oncoming traffic light to turn red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: When turning left at a traffic light, you must let pedestrians and oncoming traffic go first.

questions.question: In an accident, you must provide:

options.text: Your insurance and registration information.
Your full name and address.
Help to anyone who is injured.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must give your name, address, registration, and insurance information to other drivers. Help anyone who is injured.

questions.question: You should honk your horn when you:

options.text: Are traveling through an intersection.
Are passing a bicyclist.
See a child about to run into the street.
Are parallel parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: See a child about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn as a warning when another driver or pedestrian may not see you. For example, honk if a child is about to run into the street in front of you.

questions.question: What do large flashing arrow panels mean?

options.text: Merge into the lane the arrow points to.
Look in the direction of the arrow.
Stay in your current lane.
Stop completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge into the lane the arrow points to.
questions.explanation: Large flashing arrow panels are used in construction zones when a lane is closed. Slow down and merge in the direction the arrow shows.

questions.question: Your blind spot is the area you:

options.text: Cannot see without turning your head.
See directly behind your vehicle.
See in your rearview mirror.
See in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot see without turning your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas next to and behind your vehicle that you cannot see without turning your head.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Yield when turning left on green.
One-way traffic.
Cattle crossing.
Two-way left turn lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield when turning left on green.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers turning left at a green light to yield to oncoming traffic. You may turn left when it is safe.

questions.question: You may go through a yellow light if:

options.text: There is an emergency vehicle crossing your lane.
There are pedestrians crossing.
You are turning right.
You are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you should continue through carefully.

questions.question: If two drivers reach an open intersection at the same time:

options.text: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
The driver on the left has the right-of-way.
One driver may go without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: If you arrive at an open intersection at the same time as a vehicle on your right, yield to that vehicle. You may go when it is safe.

questions.question: Stopping distance does NOT depend on:

options.text: Your reaction time.
The time of day.
Your vehicle's brake condition.
Your vehicle's tire condition and type.

questions.correctAnswerText: The time of day.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your reaction time, weather and visibility, vehicle weight, brake condition, tire condition and type, road conditions, and speed. The time of day does not affect stopping distance.

questions.question: You may honk your horn when you:

options.text: Have to stop quickly.
Are passing another car.
Lose control of your car.
Are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lose control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. This alerts other drivers to a dangerous situation.

questions.question: To avoid headlight glare at night, look:

options.text: Straight ahead.
Over your shoulder.
At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights are too bright, keep your eyes on the right edge of the road. Do not look directly at the headlights, as the glare can blind you for several seconds.
